statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 10% sits in the low band, well below the block threshold, and the same assessment applies to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON for both instruments. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC window spanning the US cash open, the S&P Global flash PMIs and the delayed post-release second leg, where the published forecast reaches the WATCH band for two hours, and again in the 19:00 UTC power hour. Unscheduled headline risk from the Trump-Xi state visit is treated as a Stress and Confidence factor rather than an observed path amplifier. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Narrow two-way overnight rotation under a record close holds Tail at the low-band floor
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed on 22 September at 30,732.40, up 250.04 points or 0.82 percent, inside a 30,496.43-30,770.63 range and at a fresh 52-week and all-time closing high against a 22,841.42-30,770.63 annual range. Leadership was narrow rather than broad: every tracked semiconductor name finished higher while the megacap complex split roughly evenly between gainers and decliners, an AI-chip rally offsetting consumer-technology weakness. Globex NQ now trades near 31,032.50, essentially unchanged at plus 4.00 points or 0.01 percent, inside an 85-point overnight band of 30,985.25-31,070.50 that spans only about 0.27 percent. Price sits near the middle of that band, roughly 45 points above the overnight low after a genuine bounce and about 40 points below the high after fading it, which is two-way rotation rather than persistent directional efficiency. Cross-asset context is supportive but not uniformly aligned: VIX closed at 14.21, down 0.66 or 4.4 percent and near the low end of a 13.38-35.30 annual range; WTI trades near 89-90 dollars and Brent near 98-99 dollars after a sixth consecutive lower session, following the restart of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and reported progress toward ending hostilities with Iran; against that, the 2-year yield near 4.79 percent is the highest since mid-2024 and the 10-year sits just under 5.00 percent, leaving little cushion. Tokyo cash is shut for a third consecutive day for the Autumnal Equinox, so the Asian book is thin, with MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan up 0.7 percent, Korea up 1.2 percent and Taiwan up 0.9 percent. The day ahead carries European flash PMIs from 07:15 UTC, the S&P Global US flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC just after the cash open, a Fed Barr speech at 14:05 UTC, EIA inventories at 14:30 UTC and a 5-year note auction at 17:00 UTC, while President Xi begins a three-day Washington state visit whose agenda covers AI, tariffs, rare earths, the Iran war and Taiwan. Those are checkpoints and untimed headline sources, not observed structure, so they raise Stress and shape Confidence without lifting current Tail.

lookbackSummary: The last 24 published hours describe one completed US session and its orderly overnight handover. Through the European morning of 22 September Tail sat at 12-13 with Stress in the mid-30s. Tail peaked at 21 in the 14:00 UTC cash-open hour as a trend-up regime established itself, fell back to 14-17 through the mixed early afternoon, then returned to 20-21 across the 18:00-19:00 UTC power-hour block before the record close. Since the close Tail has decayed monotonically from 19 to 11 and the dominant mode has reverted from trend-up to normal, which is the decay profile of an orderly advance rather than a path that denied retracement. Every one of the 24 slots carries a published assessment, and no hour reached the blocking band.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours run from the thin late-Asian book, through the European flash PMI block, into the densest scheduled risk of the day. Tail is held at 10-13 across the Asian and European hours, where the only checkpoints are the French, German, euro-area and UK flash PMIs between 07:15 and 08:30 UTC. It steps to 21-22 for the 13:00 and 14:00 UTC hours, which cover the US cash open, the S&P Global US flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC and the delayed second-leg window that follows, giving the day's only WATCH mapping outside the close. Tail then decays to 15-18 through the US afternoon before a secondary rise to 20 in the 19:00 UTC power hour, where a record-close backdrop supports late-session extension. Overnight values return to 11-14 as Tokyo cash reopens on 24 September after three closed sessions. Every forecast value beyond the current clock hour is conditional risk, not observed structure; confidence decays from 88 to 76 across the window.
